decisive_items: marked vascularity of the mass, supplied by branches of the left superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries
irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact
response.rationale: The purplish, friable, highly vascular mass with feeding arteries strongly favors angiosarcoma over other candidates; granulomatous inflammation is nonspecific and can accompany angiosarcoma. Langerhans cell histiocytosis is a plausible alternative given the age and friable lesion, but lacks the explicit vascular supply pattern.

rejected.why: Granulomatous inflammation and pus-filled sores are nonspecific; no vascular or malignant features are explained.
Rhabdomyosarcoma is a pediatric malignancy but typically less vascular and not classically purplish-friable; atypical cells are shared.
Malignant granular cell tumor is extremely rare and lacks the vascular and bleeding phenotype.
Merkel cell carcinoma is virtually nonexistent in a 7-year-old and lacks the vascular supply description.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis can be friable and purplish, but the marked arterial supply and bleeding are more characteristic of angiosarcoma.
